28294f9dfd40589f1a343f6fd8a7f9decf0e88ac.subject: Cover every chunk-world.yml dispatch input in the Chunker Actions UI
28294f9dfd40589f1a343f6fd8a7f9decf0e88ac.body:
The GitHub Actions panel only ever sent target-format and a config blob; the
other seven workflow_dispatch inputs (world-source, world, world-repository,
prune-bounds, output-name, output, max-jobs, regions-per-shard) were silently
hard-coded in ipc.ts, so a user could never point the workflow at an existing
release asset or artifact, bound its region-planning trim, name its output, ask
for a release alongside the artifact, or tune its job/shard sizing.

ChunkerActionsPanel.vue now offers a real, validated, localized control for
every one of the ten inputs; ipc.ts validates and forwards them, skipping this
app's own upload when world-source/world point at something that already
exists, and remembers the exact dispatched output-name so collection still
finds the right archive inside the artifact regardless of what name was typed.

A new hand-written guard (scripts/check-chunker-ui-inventory.mjs, run through
workflowUiInventory.test.ts) fails when a workflow input has no matching UI
literal and dispatch literal, or the UI names an input the workflow dropped;
verified red by deleting one inventory row and green after restoring it.

呢個 GitHub Actions 面板本身淨係識送 target-format 同一舊 config，其餘七個
workflow_dispatch 輸入（world-source、world、world-repository、
prune-bounds、output-name、output、max-jobs、regions-per-shard）全部靜靜雞
喺 ipc.ts 度寫死，用家永遠冚唔到一個已經存在嘅發佈檔案或者附件，冚唔到
裁剪邊界、輸出名、要唔要順便出發佈，或者調節工作/分片大小。

而家 ChunkerActionsPanel.vue 對十個輸入每一個都有真正、有驗證、有雙語嘅
控制項；ipc.ts 會驗證同轉送呢啲值，如果 world-source/world 指緊一個已經
存在嘅嘢就唔會再自己上傳，仲會記住實際派工用嘅 output-name，等收集嗰陣
唔理輸入乜嘢名都搵到啱嘅檔案。

新增一個手寫嘅 Guard（scripts/check-chunker-ui-inventory.mjs，透過
workflowUiInventory.test.ts 執行），一發現工作流程輸入喺 UI 度冇對應控制
項同派工欄位，或者 UI 講緊一個工作流程已經冚走嘅輸入，就會爆；刪走一行
清單見到爆紅，補返見到轉綠，親眼驗證過。

ae00618d1285581214d285bf8e50c23570c1e8a7.subject: Fix three integration-tip defects: hosted classification, workflow drift, packaging split
ae00618d1285581214d285bf8e50c23570c1e8a7.body:
capabilityProfile.ts never classified chunkerActions:*, so a hosted deployment
would have refused it by pure accident of nobody writing a line down. It gets
the same opt-in github shape as its close cousin cirender -- both upload a
world/config and dispatch a GitHub Actions run, so both need the same
credential and the same honesty about needing it.

chunk-world.yml's target-format input was still free-text months after the
app's own picker grew a real 18-format enum, so a typo dispatched happily and
failed a workflow run minutes later instead of failing the dropdown instantly.
It is now a type: choice with the app's own list, byte-for-byte, so
check-workflow-drift.mjs actually has something to compare.

The packaging config had quietly grown chunk-world.yml onto the SAME
extraResources filter that CI_WORKFLOW_FILE_NAMES governs -- which sounds like
tidying up and is actually a landmine: bootstrapCiRepository() writes every
file on that list into a repository the instant somebody sets up cloud map
rendering, credentials and all, no Chunker involved. Folding a Chunker workflow
into that list would have quietly installed a world-conversion pipeline nobody
asked for onto every render bootstrap. It gets its own resources/chunk-workflow
destination instead, and chunkeractions/ipc.ts now reads from there.

capabilityProfile.ts 一直冇幫 chunkerActions:* 做分類，托管環境會因為冇人寫低
決定而預設拒絕，而唔係因為諗清楚先拒絕。而家同佢個表親 cirender 用返同一套
github opt-in 邏輯，兩個都係上傳嘢再叫 GitHub Actions 走一轉，理應要求同一個
憑證。chunk-world.yml 個 target-format 輸入仲用緊自由文字，人哋 app 個揀單
早就有齊 18 個格式，打錯字唔會即刻話你知，要等個 workflow 行到一半先炸。而家
改做 choice，同 app 個列表一字不差。打包設定仲靜雞雞將 chunk-world.yml 塞咗入
cirender 專用嗰個檔案清單度 -- 呢個唔係執靚啲，係地雷：一開部署渲染機就會將
成個轉換 workflow 唔問自取咁裝落去，跟埋憑證。而家分返開兩個目的地。

ca7dc04620acd4f4b5f92de862579083a0f6e743.subject: Two more real bugs the previous fix's own captures were still showing
ca7dc04620acd4f4b5f92de862579083a0f6e743.body:
Recapturing with --worldlens-direct-launch (as asked, after the earlier
false alarm) surfaced two real defects neither unit test nor the prior
capture pass had caught:

1. RAIL_JOB_SHORTCUT_LABELS in App.vue was a plain object literal
   calling t() once at module setup time, not a computed(). shell.ts's
   catalogue values had already moved to the new short labels
   ("Actions", "SSH", "Convert", "Servers", "Downloader"), but the
   running app kept rendering the OLD fallback strings baked into that
   one-time t() call ("GitHub Actions", "Remote SSH", "Chunker") forever -
   the catalogue update from the previous commit had no way to reach a
   value that was already computed. Wrapped it in a real computed(),
   matching the pattern `pages` already uses two lines above it, and
   updated the fallback strings to match the current catalogue values
   on principle (drift between the two was always a code smell, even
   though the computed() is what actually prevents it from mattering).

2. Even with the right labels, "Actions", "Convert" and "Backups" (7
   Latin characters each, the widest of the seven short labels) still
   rendered with an ellipsis: the compact row's 22px icon + 6px gap +
   6px padding left only ~40px for text, not enough for 7 characters
   at 11px. Tightened to an 18px icon + 4px gap + 4px padding, freeing
   the row to ~50px - found and confirmed by rebuilding and re-driving
   the real packaged app three times, not by arithmetic.

Recaptured at 1280x800 and 1280x600 with --worldlens-direct-launch
(isolated profile, confirmed via clean aria-labels like "GitHub
runners" rather than the machine's real personal-vocabulary
substitutions the previous pass caught and ruled out): both report
rail.scrollHeight === rail.clientHeight, all four destinations
rendered and within the rail's bounds, and every shortcut label reads
in full with no ellipsis - "Actions", "Docker", "SSH", "Convert",
"Backups", then "More". Captures: v5-final-01-rail-1280x800.png,
v5-final-02-rail-1280x600.png, replacing the earlier v3/v4 attempts
under wl-settings-captures, which have been deleted rather than kept
as stale evidence.

packages/ui typecheck clean; 368/368 relevant tests still pass (no
test needed changing - the bug was in application wiring the tests
never exercised, not in the catalogue values or the character-count
bound itself).

執到嘢喇（又一次）- 個字典啱晒，個掣顯示緊嗰句就係唔啱，因為攞字嗰下淨係執行一次，
之後個字典點改都追唔到。仲有,七個字母嘅字喺嗰行度真係唔夠位,唔係計錯數，係真係窄。

ed5ff28c2c629bb2c2a1f57040d8675a51d0744f.subject: Give every rail shortcut its own short label, not an ellipsis on the full one
ed5ff28c2c629bb2c2a1f57040d8675a51d0744f.body:
v3-fixed-01/02's own captures showed "Remo…", "Chun…", "Back…" and
"Der …" - the full job title truncating mid-word inside the compact
row's 80px column. A visible label nobody can read is a clipping
defect, not a compact row, and Material navigation rails are supposed
to carry short single-line labels in the first place - reaching for
the full title there was the actual mistake, not the column width.

rail.shortcut.* in shell.ts now holds seven dedicated short labels
(Actions, Docker, SSH, Convert, Backups, Servers, Downloader in
English; 操作, Docker, SSH, 轉換, 備份, 伺服器, 下載器 in Cantonese),
each within ~10 Latin or ~4 CJK characters with no ellipsis anywhere.
The button's accessible name and tooltip are untouched - they still
carry the full job title from tabs.page.* beside these, so nothing
about "what this button does" got shorter, only what's printed on it.

railShortcutLabels.test.ts enforces the bound two ways: directly on
the catalogue entries (existence, non-empty, length, no ellipsis) and
on a real mounted AppRail's rendered .wl-rail-label text for every
configured shortcut. jsdom cannot measure real layout - scrollWidth
and clientWidth are always zero there, same limitation
railOverflow.test.ts already documents - so the scrollWidth <=
clientWidth assertion is included honestly as a trivially-true check
in this environment, and the character-count bound is what actually
catches a regression: watched red with cirender's label swapped back
to "GitHub Actions rendering console" (both the catalogue test and the
mounted-render test failed), restored, watched green.

packages/ui typecheck clean. 368/368 relevant tests pass across 38
files (15 new).

七個捷徑，七個度身訂造嘅短名 - 唔再係讀到一半斷晒尾嗰種，靠個 tooltip
兜返轉頭嗰種。個掣做緊乜嘢一個字都冇改，改嘅淨係印喺面嗰行字。

dc958181f5e3b21271999e995ad82a5e96267675.subject: Anchor the changelog trailer guard to line starts
dc958181f5e3b21271999e995ad82a5e96267675.body:
The guard refused any body containing "Co-Authored-By:", which is exactly the phrase one
commit quotes in prose while describing the trailer leak it fixed. A trailer is a
Key: value line at the start of a line, so the guard now matches that shape, and proves
its own matcher on a synthetic trailer and a quoted sentence before sweeping the data,
so a mangled regex cannot pass quietly.

個 Guard 見到 "Co-Authored-By:" 就 fail，但有條 commit 係引住呢句嚟講佢修咗嘅
trailer 漏洞。Trailer 係行首嘅 Key: value，而家就對住呢個形狀查；掃資料之前先用一條
假 trailer 同一句引文自證，regex 寫壞咗都唔會靜靜地綠。

d72cecc430a480ef62fc323a9f19197e740fcceb.subject: Give the rail shortcuts, without lying about what four means
d72cecc430a480ef62fc323a9f19197e740fcceb.body:
The user asked for GitHub Actions, Docker hosting, remote SSH, Chunker,
Backups, Minecraft servers and the world downloader on the left rail.
AppRail.vue's old doc comment claimed four destinations was a hard
cap; reading shellNavigation.ts and featureTargets.ts showed that cap
is about RailDestination (home/map/host/work) - which screen the shell
switches to - and is a real, separate concern from a one-click path to
a job that already lives in Work. So RailDestination stays exactly
four, and the rail gained a second, distinct list: jobShortcuts, each
one calling the same open-page route the command palette's own
"open a page" row already uses.

AppRail.vue: new jobShortcuts prop, openJob emit, a visually separated
second <ul> below the four destinations, same button markup, same
48px target, same accessible-name pattern. App.vue: a hand-written
RAIL_JOB_SHORTCUT_IDS list (deliberately not derived from jobRegistry,
so a job never grows the rail by existing - see the doc comment) feeding
a railJobShortcuts computed, wired to the real AppRail instance.

railJobShortcutInventory.test.ts locks the exact seven ids by reading
App.vue's real source - watched red with worldDownloader removed from
the list, restored, watched green. shellAccessibility.test.ts gained
four new AppRail tests: shortcuts render as real labelled buttons,
clicking one emits openJob (never select) with the right id, and every
shortcut stays in plain keyboard tab order. Added the missing
tabs.page.worldDownloader catalogue entry chrome.ts needed once the
new pages-array row started rendering it. Added one paragraph to the
command-palette site article naming the same trade-off. packages/ui
and packages/site both typecheck clean; 258/259 UI copy tests and
55/55 site content tests pass (the one pre-existing failure is
components/world, untouched, unrelated, and outside this lane).

用戶要嘅七樣嘢,而家個 rail 度真係撳得到 - 冇呃人講「四個就係上限」,
因為嗰個「四」講緊嘅係另一件事,唔係呢件。

400fc2844941e887ee379f7da782ad595ffc9f53.subject: Real M3 card group anatomy for Settings, plus a genuine narrow-window Clipping found and fixed
400fc2844941e887ee379f7da782ad595ffc9f53.body:
The first pass at this only bumped padding numbers, which the coordinator
correctly called a tweak rather than the asked-for Material Design 3 revamp.
SettingsSection.vue's card is now built from the real M3 token layer
instead of hand-picked pixel values: title-medium/body-medium typescale
for the header, surface-container for the card fill, outline-variant for
the divider between stacked cards, and a new exported .mb-setting__row
list-item utility (56px minimum, leading-icon/content/trailing grid, a
state layer drawn from the M3 hover/pressed opacity tokens) for any card
whose body is a stack of simple rows. The settings search-match list in
AppSettings.vue now uses that same row anatomy instead of its own
hand-rolled hover tint. The docked-left vertical tab strip with
aria-orientation and the anchored regex-searchable search field were
already correctly implemented and needed no rework.

Every individual settings row in this dialog (theme picker, size dial,
download concurrency, Java runtime, storage) genuinely needs multi-line
supporting text, hints and provenance lines per this project's own
settings-explanation rules, so forcing them into rigid single-line 56px
rows would have fought that requirement rather than served it - they stay
full-width M3 card content, which is itself a legitimate M3 pattern, and
that trade-off is recorded honestly rather than papered over with a
row wrapper that does not fit what it wraps.

Built the whole workspace (@worldlens/design-system, @worldlens/shared,
then `pnpm -r build`) and drove the real Electron app through the cheap
Lowlevel headless route end to end: real onboarding clicks, real Settings
open, real CDP-driven viewport and theme/language changes. That surfaced
a genuine defect no source read would have caught: at a 320px window,
the tab strip's fixed 10rem minimum width left the detail pane so little
room that its new title-medium heading broke every character of "Mojang
download consent" onto its own line. Fixed with a narrow-width floor and
re-captured the same tuple to confirm real word-wrapping. Verified clean
at 320px and normal desktop width, English and bilingual, dark and light.

Added a source-level regression pinning that narrow-width floor (watched
it fail against the old 10rem value, then pass), a card-anatomy test for
the new token-drawn padding/gap/divider, and a check that Settings never
opts the strip out of its default vertical placement. Updated the token
name one earlier test still asserted after the surface-container/
outline-variant tokens replaced the hand-mixed rgba tint. Documented the
new layout in docs/display-and-ease-of-use.md, the closest existing
article to AppSettings.vue's own display section - no dedicated
Settings-dialog article existed to update.

check-webapp-parity.mjs stayed green throughout, including a full
BlueMap-Material submodule checkout so it actually inspects all four
surfaces instead of skipping silently.

上次淨係郁咗 padding 數字，人哋話得啱：嗰啲叫調校，唔叫翻新。今次真係用返
M3 嘅 token 起卡片，仲喺 320px 度捉到一個字拆一行嘅笑話，修返好之後親眼
影相確認直情摺得返。

1b63fd348bf852a6fe3950ade8e1c425a4075dfd.subject: Fix regex-builder popover crash, sweep clipped card titles, revamp Settings card spacing
1b63fd348bf852a6fe3950ade8e1c425a4075dfd.body:
Refs #175: opening the settings search field's regex builder could crash
the renderer in a packaged build. ConfigRegexBuilder is v-menu popover
content Vuetify repositions with a ResizeObserver on every resize; a
max-height/overflow-y:auto card whose text sits near that cap is the
textbook setup for a scrollbar-toggle layout loop (scrollbar width changes
the content box, which reflows wrapped text past/under the cap, which
toggles the scrollbar again, forever) - and Vuetify's own flip-loop guard
only watches for an alternating boolean, not a plain width oscillation, so
nothing there catches it. scrollbar-gutter: stable reserves the track
unconditionally and removes the toggle. Applied the same defensive fix to
the two other anchored, scrollable popovers with the identical shape
(TabGroupPicker, TabStrip). Added a regression test that mounts the field,
clicks the affordance, and asserts the popover actually renders instead of
hanging.

Clipping sweep: sixteen more v-card-title elements across the config,
project, remote and mounts screens were still sitting on Vuetify's default
overflow:hidden/white-space:nowrap/text-overflow:ellipsis, the exact
truncation this codebase had already fixed once in
DependencyInstallerPanel.vue - a translated title long enough for
bilingual mode or Cantonese was silently clipped with no ellipsis painted.
Fixed all sixteen with the same white-space:normal/overflow-wrap:anywhere
pattern, routed around v-dialog/v-menu teleport boundaries where present.
Audited every other capped/scrollable overlay in settings, tabs and config
for a missing overflow-y:auto (none found - the rest of this app already
gets that right).

Settings dialog: .mb-setting shipped at 16px padding / 12px gap, which is
exactly what "a bit cramped" describes for a Material Design 3 card. Bumped to the
M3 24px/16px card anatomy and added a token-drawn divider between stacked
sections. Tab strip docking, vertical aria-orientation and search-wired
regex builders were already implemented correctly in TabStrip/
TabbedNavigation and needed no change. Two new source-level tests pin the
padding/gap numbers and the divider rule so a later edit cannot quietly
revert them.

check-webapp-parity.mjs verified green with the BlueMap submodule actually
checked out (was silently skipping the whole check before).

執到少少 Clipping 同一個會撞爛個 popover 嘅 resize 死循環,順手幫 Settings
嘅卡片鬆返鬆啲,唔使成日撞埋一堆。scrollbar 開開關關撞出嚟嗰種死循環,診斷都
幾考功夫,一個 CSS 屬性就搞掂,笑死。

c65df076ccecd197f472b538d92795ec76b60a3d.subject: Finish Chunker review fixes: schema editor types, i18n, cleanup
c65df076ccecd197f472b538d92795ec76b60a3d.body:
Turns the seven-error UI type-check red into a clean 0 for the ui package
(app package's remaining six are pre-existing mcserver defects, byte-identical
to main, and out of this lane's scope). ChunkerSchemaEditor.vue reads a
non-optional nestingLevel computed instead of arithmetic on an optional prop;
ChunkerScreen.vue's convert request omits inputFormat entirely instead of
handing exactOptionalPropertyTypes an explicit undefined; the never-imported
ChunkerValueEditor.vue is gone.

Also gives the schema editor its first-ever t() call -- it shipped with zero
localized strings, every label and hint hardcoded in English -- and finally
wires the recovery controls' search/select/empty/no-match labels that had
been sitting unlocalized next to search-label props that already used t().
Seven orphaned chunker.editor.* catalogue keys that outlived the component
they were written for are swept out too.

執到七個型別錯誤跌返做零：schema editor 唔再靠一個得意但可能係 undefined 嘅
depth做算術，而係讀一個穩陣嘅 nestingLevel；convert request 唔再塞一個
undefined 落去話明唔准 undefined 嘅欄位，直接唔攞就得；冇人 import 過嘅
ChunkerValueEditor.vue 都送走咗。仲執埋 schema editor 成頁英文冇翻譯、
recovery 掣同揀嘢揀漏咗嘅翻譯，順手清埋七條冇人叫過嘅殘留翻譯key。

79e27c48bbb77b71d8013ecbcd234101b9de88f2.subject: Record the 1 GB and 10 GB smoke test, and what it measured
79e27c48bbb77b71d8013ecbcd234101b9de88f2.body:
Two synthetic worlds from the committed worldgen, both measured rather than estimated. The
1 GB rendered clean in 59.5 minutes - 62,354 tiles, 2.49 GB out - and passed the shipped
static-host validator, which is the first time that tool has been run against a real
multi-gigabyte map rather than a fixture.

The 10 GB was stopped at 6.75%, deliberately and with nothing failing. It had produced
43,349 tiles and was reporting an ETA consistent with the 1 GB run, which is the useful
number: roughly an hour per gigabyte of world on this machine, single process. Recorded that
way rather than left to look like an abandoned run.

GitHub Actions is verified end to end with a 103 MB map artifact and a receipt carrying a real
plan fingerprint, and the world it rendered is published so the run repeats. Docker is
blocked on a service that needs elevation, and the LAN hosts were deliberately not used as a
substitute because each is running somebody else workloads.

兩個世界都係度出嚟嘅數，唔係估。10 GB 停喺 6.75% 係特登，唔係壞咗 - 夠數推算就夠。

cccade075ead063984351a1b6075bea246ce11b1.subject: Record the preserved primary-checkout work, without taking it
cccade075ead063984351a1b6075bea246ce11b1.body:
Merged with the ours strategy, deliberately, and that choice is the whole content of this
commit so it is worth being explicit about.

The preserved branch holds what the primary Worktree was carrying uncommitted: a
describe-jars change naming the fork as the source repository, and a submodule pointer at
a3b2d9eb. Both are already here and both are already better. The describe-jars fix is
identical except for four lines of comment, where this branch's wording says CI staged the
jar and then refused it and main's says CI built it correctly and then refused to stage it -
main describes the failure in the right order. The submodule here is 7e7cfd03, which is
newer than a3b2d9eb and contains it.

So an ordinary merge would take a worse comment and an older submodule, which is a
regression dressed as integration. Ours keeps main's content and still makes the preserved
commit an ancestor, so the history survives permanently in this repository's own graph and
the branch can be retired without losing the record.

The comparison that justifies this was run rather than assumed: the two files were read and
diffed byte for byte, and the submodule ancestry was checked, before anything was merged.

用 ours strategy 特登唔攞佢啲改動 - 因為 main 入面已經有，而且寫得好過佢。噉樣段歷史
留得低，個 branch 又刪得，兩樣都唔使犧牲。

a16046a7ca5ea89b0fcbd2905c0f8fbb650d9481.subject: Preserve what the primary checkout was holding, before it moves to main
a16046a7ca5ea89b0fcbd2905c0f8fbb650d9481.body:
Two changes were sitting uncommitted in the primary Worktree, and both turn out to be
superseded rather than lost. They are committed here anyway, because the difference between
"superseded" and "lost" is a comparison somebody has to actually run, and a cleanup that
assumes the first is how the second happens.

The describe-jars change names the fork rather than upstream as the source repository, which
is correct - the jars are built from the fork and their embedded webapp carries this
project's Material Design 3 interface. That fix is already on main. The only difference is
four lines of comment wording, and main's phrasing is the better of the two: it says CI
built the jar correctly and then refused to stage it, where this one says CI staged it and
then refused it, which describes the failure in the wrong order.

The submodule pointer here is a3b2d9eb. Main is already at 7e7cfd03, which is newer and
includes it.

So nothing here is unique. Recorded rather than discarded, and the comparison that
establishes it is written down so nobody has to trust that it was made.

主 checkout 度有兩樣未 commit 嘅嘢，查過之後兩樣 main 都已經有咗，而且寫得仲好。照樣
commit 低先，因為「已經有」同「唔見咗」係要真係比較過先知，唔係靠估。

325e18a311aeb17cfbb85b13b938ce113c16be10.subject: Run the purity guard from the suite, and prove it both ways
325e18a311aeb17cfbb85b13b938ce113c16be10.body:
It was an npm script, which means it ran when somebody remembered. GitHub Actions runs no
tests and gates nothing here, so a check living only in CI would never run at all and one
living only in a script runs about as often. A guard nobody runs is decoration, and this
one guards drift that is invisible by nature: a hardcoded colour renders perfectly, it is
simply the one thing on the page ignoring the reader's theme.

Four tests, and two of them are the pair that matters. One writes an undeclared colour where
the guard actually looks and asserts it is refused by name; the other writes the same colour
with a declaration and asserts it is accepted. Without the second, a guard that refused
everything would pass the first, and an exemption route that had quietly stopped working
would make the guard unusable rather than strict. The probe is removed in a finally, so a
failure cannot leave the tree dirty.

Writing them found a real hole in the guard. Its skip patterns used a character class
meaning 'either separator', that class lost a backslash on its way through tooling, and the
survivor matched only forward slashes - so on Windows the generated-theme directory was
never skipped at all and the seed colour every role is derived from was reported as a
violation. Paths are normalised to forward slashes before matching now, so a pattern never
has to know about separators.

之前個 guard 要人記得先行到。而家跟住測試行，仲要證明佢兩邊都work: 冇聲明就一定紅，
聲明咗就一定綠。

59b3b79412bde3c04e3bceb51ab604c949e5752b.subject: Pure Material Design 3 on every surface, with the exemptions written down
59b3b79412bde3c04e3bceb51ab604c949e5752b.body:
The guard covered the map and nothing else, so the map was the one surface that had already
been cleaned and the other three were where the undeclared colour actually was. It now runs
over the map webapp, the documentation site, the desktop interface and the render page,
because the rule applies to each surface individually rather than to the project as a whole -
that aggregate reading is exactly what lets one corner sit outside it.

210 findings became 13 real ones as the categories separated, and the separation is the work.
148 were the CSS named-colour table, which is not a file containing colour data but a file
that *is* colour data - replacing a literal there would make the translator report a
different colour than the one it was asked about. The creative studio, the marker studio and
the logo canvas hold colours somebody chose for their own artwork, which must not shift when
the theme does. The hue wheel's red is the hue red: it is the value being offered, not a
colour picked to display it. The picker's thumb has to stay visible against every colour a
person can select, including the palette's own, so a role there would vanish over its own
value.

Every one of those now says so in place, and the file-level marker exists because 148
line-level ones would have buried the table they were annotating.

The one real fix left in the site: the rainbow animation was four hand-picked stops. It
walks the hue circle now, at a constant saturation and lightness, so it no longer dims at
whichever stop happened to be darkest - and it leaves no literal to drift from the palette.
Its reduced-motion state already settled on one colour rather than slowing down, which is
the part that matters; that colour is now the palette's primary, so it reads as a choice
rather than as something that failed to load.

Broke it with a new undeclared colour in a stylesheet and watched it named with its exact
line, then green on restore.

之前得個地圖有人睇住，所以另外三個介面先係真係有嘢漏。而家四個都睇。210 個報告分完類
淨返 13 個係真嘢 - 其餘係色本身就係資料，唔係裝飾。

41970600df414e856bcf1adad1951d00e08c5e3d.subject: Pure Material Design 3 across every surface, and a guard that will not accept prose
41970600df414e856bcf1adad1951d00e08c5e3d.body:
The audit found colour that was not a palette role on all four surfaces, and the fixes fall
into two kinds. Real violations: the site's contract page had a hand-picked teal accent,
which was the one colour on that page ignoring the visitor's theme, and its camera preview
and the gallery's image backing were both flat #111. All three now take roles.

Genuine data keeps its colour and now says why: the console's warning colours are a status
palette and Material Design 3 has no warning role, so one has to be chosen; the QR code is
deliberately not themed because a camera needs true dark-on-light and tinting it into the
palette would make it prettier and sometimes unreadable.

My own render page was the worst of it. It had 26 tokens and no state layers, no elevation
and no 48px target - tokens without anatomy, which is a page that has the colours of
Material Design 3 without being it. It now has a real filled button: the state layer drawn
as a pseudo-element at the specified opacities rather than a second hand-picked colour, the
pill at 40px with the touch target at 48px around it, cards at elevation 1, and motion that
stops when the reader has asked for less.

The guard's first version matched the prose of the comment above a line, so whether an
exemption counted depended on which synonym somebody reached for - a comment saying 'data
encoding' was refused while 'data colour' passed, and neither author would have known why.
It now requires an explicit material-exempt: marker, so an exemption is deliberate rather
than accidentally phrased.

One test I added passed for the wrong reason and I nearly kept it. A backslash eaten on the
way through a script turned its word boundary into a literal backspace character, so it
matched a hex literal followed by a control character - which never occurs, so it could not
have failed. Repaired, then broken on purpose with a real hardcoded colour to watch it go
red before trusting it.

唔再靠估你寫咗咩字，要寫明 material-exempt: 先算數。

fd4187e5654cbbb5bedfd3ce8b1d2794ea41c56d.subject: Nothing was watching the map's Material Design 3 layer
fd4187e5654cbbb5bedfd3ce8b1d2794ea41c56d.body:
The GitHub Pages site has had a hand-written fail-closed inventory for a while. The map's
webapp had none at all - so its whole Material Design 3 layer could have vanished with
nothing going red. That is not a hypothetical: every file it lives in is a file upstream
also owns, so an upstream merge is precisely how it would go.

Eight contracts, written out rather than discovered. A check that enumerates what it finds
and then validates it passes cleanly on a webapp that has none of this, because it would
find nothing and validate nothing.

Each row counts files, not declarations. A token declared and used nowhere is a token the
interface does not render, and taking the call sites while leaving the definitions is
exactly the shape of a bad merge.

Two breaks, and the first one taught me something. Renaming the token declarations left
the guard green, because nine call sites still matched - but that loss breaks the SCSS
build loudly anyway, so it is not the one to guard. The realistic loss is the reverse:
stripping the token out of eight component files, which still looks right on screen and is
silent. That went red naming the contract and the count, and green on restore. I checked
the exit code directly rather than through a pipe, which had been reporting 0 over a
genuine failure.

Skips rather than fails without the submodule. A clone without --recurse-submodules has no
webapp, and complaining there would be a complaint about the clone.

5461fdb5eef97acc2ecb63ca078e49b93cea9a13.subject: School mode was shipped on the site and absent from the inventory
5461fdb5eef97acc2ecb63ca078e49b93cea9a13.body:

Also withdrawing something I wrote in this file an hour ago. I said the GitHub Pages site
carried 'only some' of the contracts. It carries 52 in a hand-written fail-closed
inventory plus 13 more in a second one, including the toy locks, the authenticator and

the result as fact. The corrected entry names the five gaps that are actually there,
including that the Material Design 3 webapp has no inventory at all, which makes it the surface
furthest from parity rather than the site.

30c5f946826b8b8817317831b12cc05b0a60dd83.subject: Tick what actually landed, and say plainly what did not

184b0eff720515f8f4631d727d0337214f51d76f.subject: The workflow was converting worlds with a Chunker nine versions older than the app
184b0eff720515f8f4631d727d0337214f51d76f.body:
Adding the version claim found a live one immediately. The app bundles Chunker 1.19.1,
pinned to an exact published asset and digest, and that is what ships to people. The
workflow was downloading 1.10.0. Nine minor versions apart, on the same worlds, with
nothing on either side stating its version - so a world coming back subtly different
from one route than the other would never have been traced to this.

The app wins, because it is the thing people install and because the whole point of
this work is that GitHub Actions follows the app rather than leading it. Workflow
and submodule both move to 1.19.1.

The claim I wrote first compared the submodule with the workflow and would have sailed
straight past this, since it never looked at the app at all. It does now, and the app
is checked first: a guard that agrees with two out of three is worse than none, because
it reports clean while the disagreement that matters walks past. Reproduced the real
drift by putting 1.10.0 back, watched it name both versions and the line, restored.

be35fac8b85f1cd5132b06ee5091661701edea70.subject: Commit the world-backup record into the repository, not only onto releases
be35fac8b85f1cd5132b06ee5091661701edea70.body:
Rendering already leaves a backup behind: the world is packed, split and published
as release assets with a Cheap LFS pointer and a backup.json sidecar, on a release
nothing in this codebase can delete or overwrite.

What was missing is any record of it in the repository. catalog.ts answers 'what
backups exist' by listing releases over the network every time, so the answer needs
a connection, a credential that can still see the repository, and GitHub being up.
Clone the repository and you have no idea what is in it - a strange property for a
backup, since the thing you reach for when something has gone wrong is the thing
that only exists while everything is working.

So the pointer is committed too. A pointer is a few hundred bytes naming the
release, the asset, the size and the hash; it is designed to stand in for the large
binary, which is exactly what a committed record needs to be. git clone now brings
the map of every world backup with it.

The bytes written are the uploader's, passed through unaltered, and a caller that
supplies anything else is refused - the format is a shipped contract shared with a
sibling application and its own module says not to invent near-misses of it.
Everything this project wants to say about a backup goes in the index beside it,
for the same reason the sidecar exists.

The commit is optimistic and the conflict is expected. Appending means two renders
finishing together race, and the loser would otherwise overwrite the winner with an
index that never knew about it - the worst outcome for a record whose whole job is
not to lose things. It re-reads and retries on the typed conflict, a bounded number
of times, and a failure never fails the render: the world is already durable by
then, and trading that for a missing convenience would be a bad bargain.

render 本來就已經留低咗個 backup 喺 release，但 Repository 入面完全冇記錄，要上網
問先知有咩。而家連 pointer 都 commit 埋，clone 落嚟就見到。兩個 render 一齊完會
爭，所以係重讀再試，唔會蓋咗人哋嗰個。

7de6d9e1ae1bebce249bb991a609660d8d6c948e.subject: Make the workflows follow the app instead of restating where it lives
7de6d9e1ae1bebce249bb991a609660d8d6c948e.body:
The workflows are full of facts about this repository that they cannot check.
design/packages/app appears as a literal string a dozen times in ci.yml alone.
node-version: 22 is copied into all eight workflows while the real constraint
lives in engines.node. The product name is duplicated out of the packaging config
by hand. None of it is wrong today; all of it goes wrong silently the moment
somebody moves a package or bumps a runtime, and the first thing that notices is
a red run minutes into CI, a long way from the change that caused it.

workflow-manifest.mjs discovers those facts rather than restating them. Packages
are found by the name in their own package.json, walking the pnpm workspace
globs, so renaming a directory changes nothing and renaming a package fails
loudly - which is the right way round. The Node major comes from engines.node.
The product name, artifact name and the three managed workflow file names come
from electron-builder.config.cjs, which is required rather than parsed: its module
body only touches CSC_* variables and exports a static literal, and a regex parse
would have to re-implement string escaping and would miss the day one of those
values is computed. The env mutation is snapshotted and restored, so importing it
into a test worker cannot leak it.

check-workflow-drift.mjs compares what the workflows say against what the manifest
finds, and reports each disagreement as a file, a line and the edit that fixes it.
Its inventory of checked facts is hand-written on purpose: a rule that only
checked the paths it happened to find would pass just as cleanly on a workflow
that had stopped mentioning the app at all.

It runs locally, deliberately. GitHub Actions runs no tests and gates nothing here,
so a check living only in CI would never run; one living only in an npm script
would run only when somebody remembered. workflowDrift.test.ts spawns it from the
suite - spawns rather than imports, because scripts/ is outside design/ and Vite's
server.fs.allow refuses the import in a way that reads as a resolution failure
rather than a boundary.

Proven by breaking it. Moving design/packages/app to design/packages/desktop-shell
turns the check red with 13 named disagreements and exit 1, and turns the vitest
gate red too; moving it back returns both to green with no tracked change. Bumping
engines.node to 24 catches all 16 stale node-version pins the same way.

啲 workflow 寫死咗 app 喺邊、Node 幾多版，改個名就靜靜雞爛咗，要等 CI 行到一半先
知。而家改成自己去揾：靠 package name 唔靠路徑。試過真係搬走個 app，13 個地方即
刻紅，搬返去又綠返。

a8e36ce93b425014ef8b213e4fc63ca408ed1cea.subject: Record the two suite failures that outlive this work

Worktree here, so it will bite the next person who makes one.

e00bcd2c541b683163a06979db5906458bd3e1f8.subject: Say when this build was made, and refuse to guess when it does not know
e00bcd2c541b683163a06979db5906458bd3e1f8.body:
About printed a version and stopped there, which is half an answer: two builds a week
apart can carry the same version string whenever a release cadence pauses, and the
version alone cannot tell them apart. So the page now states when this exact build was
made, in the reader's own timezone, to the second, with the zone named.

Where the instant comes from matters more than that it appears. It is frozen into the
bundle by esbuild at build time, from the committer date of the exact commit being
built, and it is deterministic: two builds of one commit agree, and anybody can check it
with `git show`. What it is emphatically not is `new Date()` at run time, which is the
launch time of a binary that may have sat on a disk for a month and would render as a
confident fact that is simply false. There is deliberately no such fallback anywhere in
this path, and a comment beside the resolver says so, because that single line is the
whole difference between provenance and decoration and it is the line somebody will be
tempted to add the first time they meet an unavailable state.

Three states, kept distinct rather than collapsed into two: a recorded instant, an
honest "build time not recorded" for a source export with no git history to read, and
silence when the shell is simply too old to have been asked. The third is not the second.

Two defects found by looking at what actually rendered rather than at the code:

`Intl.DateTimeFormat` refuses to combine `dateStyle`/`timeStyle` with `timeZoneName` and
throws. Written the tidy way, the catch below swallowed that throw on every single call
and rendered a raw ISO string instead of local time, which reads as a deliberate format
rather than a branch that never once succeeded. Now built from component options, and
asserted on the rendered output rather than on the intent.

And this file's own test suite had all thirteen tests failing before any of this, on
`[Vuetify] Could not find defaults instance`, because the page renders real Vuetify
components while the test never installed the plugin its neighbours install. Repaired,
so the five new cases actually run rather than joining a file nobody could have noticed
was red. All 18 pass. The negative one is the one that matters: a build with no recorded
time must never show the current year.

Verified in the built bundle, not just in the tests: the main bundle carries
`builtAt: "2026-08-25T05:04:33.000Z"`, which is exactly HEAD's committer date.

About 之前淨係寫住版本號，其實講咗一半。同一個版本號可以係隔一個禮拜整嘅兩個 build，
淨睇個號分唔到邊個係邊個。而家會講埋幾時整，用你自己個時區，準到秒，仲寫埋時區名。
個時間係 build 嗰陣入面焗死嘅，用嗰個 commit 嘅日期，任何人 `git show` 都對得返。
最緊要係：唔會用 `new Date()`。嗰個係你㩒開個程式嗰刻，唔係整佢嗰刻，扮到似層層咁但係假嘅。
搵到兩個蟲：Intl 唔畀 dateStyle 同 timeZoneName 一齊用，會直接掟錯，之前個 catch 幫佢
食晒，所以次次都靜靜雞出返個 ISO 字串當係「格式」。仲有呢個 test 檔本身十三個測試全部都紅緊，
因為冇裝 Vuetify plugin，順手執返，唔係我加嗰五個測試都係入去陪紅。

2c2769ccda9a6ad07f9e7c8e1ccdbf405b99c6be.subject: Give adoption the candidate browser its button always implied
2c2769ccda9a6ad07f9e7c8e1ccdbf405b99c6be.body:
Clicking "Adopt an existing container" could do nothing at all, and the design
prototype had already written that down as a known gap: "Adoption is built, but
the button is not wired ... Clicking it today opens nothing and shows no error."

The whole defect was four lines in App.vue. It called adoptDiscover(), read
discovered.ok ? discovered.value?.[0] : undefined, and returned early when
that was falsy. Three failures, and every one of them looks identical from the
outside, which is why this survived so long.

It dropped the Answer's failure, so a build that has not wired the namespace, a
refused Docker permission and a machine with no containers on it were the same
event. It returned early with no dialog and no message, so a live-looking
control did nothing and said nothing. And it took index zero, so a machine with
three adoptable containers offered exactly one of them and never mentioned the
other two.

AdoptionBrowser.vue is the missing step. It owns discovery and has to answer for
every outcome: in flight, failed with the store's own sentence and a way to try
again, empty with what would be here and where it comes from, or the full list
with nothing hidden and nothing chosen on the user's behalf. Flavour and version
are guesses in the type, so they read as guesses on screen, and when neither can
be guessed it says so rather than leaving a gap. It carries its own search with
the anchored regex builder, like every other list in this application, and every
row is a real button.

It is mounted at all three sites the review dialog is mounted at, because a
shell variant with the dialog and no browser is a variant where the original
defect is still alive in one corner.

adoptionBrowser.contract.test.ts holds both halves, because the component can be
honest while the shell never asks it. It was proven red four separate ways
before this landed: the browser showing only the first candidate, the browser
swallowing the failure, the shell going back to index zero, and one shell
variant losing its browser. Each turned green again when restored.

One thing worth recording for whoever writes the next source-reading guard. The
first version of the App.vue assertion failed immediately, on the comment that
explains the fix rather than on any code, because the comment quotes the old
line. It strips comments now. A guard that cannot tell code from prose punishes
documenting the change.

Verified: 98 typecheck errors in the ui package before this change and 98 after,
the same ones. mcserver and App suites 13 failed before and 13 failed after, the
same ones, with 7 new passing tests on top. Nothing here fixes those 13; they
predate it.

撳「Adopt an existing container」可以完全冇反應，而原型早就寫低咗呢個係已知
問題。成件事得四行：攞完 adoptDiscover() 就直接讀 value?.[0]，冇嘢就靜靜雞
return。三個錯，喺外面睇全部一模一樣，所以先會拖到而家。

Answer 入面個 failure 掉咗，所以「呢個 build 未接通」、「Docker 冇權限」同
「部機真係冇容器」變成同一件事；提早 return 即係粒掣扮live但乜都唔做又乜都
唔講；攞 index 0 即係部機有三個容器都只俾你掂到一個，仲唔會話你知有另外兩個。

新嘅 AdoptionBrowser 要為每一個結果負責：搵緊、失敗（照搬 store 嗰句原話，
再俾條路重試）、真係空（講明本來會有乜、由邊度嚟）、或者成張清單全部列出。
猜出嚟嘅 flavour 同 version 一定要睇得出係猜。三個掛載點全部都有，因為淨係
少一個地方，嗰個角落就仲係原本嗰粒壞掉嘅掣。

cda9d25b249b6fcf60358183dcef0ed5d16865ef.subject: Replace informal house wording with plain terms and add an externally-configured wording guard
cda9d25b249b6fcf60358183dcef0ed5d16865ef.body:
The repository is public, and a set of informal internal shorthand terms had
leaked into tracked prose: comments, handoff and roadmap notes, test fixtures,
and a handful of commit messages that the generated changelog copies verbatim.
None of it changed behaviour -- it was all prose, log strings, and one code
marker (the Material Design 3 purity guard's own exemption marker, which
carried the same shorthand baked into a literal string used across twenty-odd
files) -- so every occurrence is swapped for the ordinary English word it
already stood for: a clipping defect stays a clipping defect, a guard stays a
guard, GitHub Actions stays GitHub Actions.

Renamed materialPurity.test.ts to materialPurity.test.ts and its internal
"pure-material-design"/"material-exempt:" markers to "pure-material-design"/
"material-exempt:", updating every file that declares an exemption with the
old marker and every doc that named the old filename.

The generated changelog is derived from git history, and history is immutable
here, so a handful of old commit subjects and bodies still carry the old
wording verbatim. Added scripts/changelog-overrides.json: a committed,
per-commit-SHA map of neutral subject/body text that build-changelog.mjs
consults before falling back to the raw commit message (and before the
existing full-redaction list), so the published changelog and its in-app
viewer read cleanly without rewriting a single commit. Filled it for every
commit a full-history sweep found still carrying the old wording.

Added scripts/check-private-terms.mjs: a fail-closed sibling to the existing
check-published-text.mjs, reading its term list from a file outside this
repository named by WORLDLENS_PRIVATE_TERMS_FILE. With that variable unset --
the case on every public machine, including CI -- it prints one line saying it
skipped and exits 0. With it set, it scans every tracked file and fails naming
file:line for any hit, and separately reports (without failing) any of the
last 200 commit subjects that still carry the old wording, pointing at the
overrides file as the fix. Wired as `check:private-terms` in design/
package.json, documented in AGENTS.md, and covered by a vitest wrapper that
exercises the skip path (the only path a shared checkout can exercise without
holding the private term list itself).

Verified: the guard reports clean on this tree with a real term list supplied
via the environment variable, and correctly fails naming the exact file and
line when a term is deliberately reintroduced. build-changelog.mjs --check,
lint-workflows.mjs, and the site's article-bundle assertion all still pass;
the renamed and new test files pass under vitest.

換走啲平時傾偈用嘅代號，改用正正常常嘅字，仲加多個睇門口嘅工具

呢個 repo 係公開嘅，一批平時內部傾偈用開嘅代號漏咗入去 - 留喺註解、交更同
路線圖筆記、測試固件，仲有幾個 commit message（生成嘅 changelog 會照抄）。
冇一樣係改緊行為，全部係文字、log 字串，同一個寫死喺代碼度嘅標記（個
Material Design 3 純度 guard 自己嗰個 exemption 標記，本來個代號直情焗死喺
廿幾個檔案入面嘅一個字串），所以逐個換返做本身代表嘅普通英文字。

個 materialPurity.test.ts 改咗名做 materialPurity.test.ts，入面嘅標記同埋
成廿幾個檔案入面嗰個 exemption 標記都跟住改，舊檔名喺文檔度提到嘅都改晒。

Changelog 係跟住 commit history 生成嘅，而歷史喺呢度係唔郁得，所以有幾個
舊 commit 嘅 subject 同 body 仍然係照字咁講嗰套。加咗
scripts/changelog-overrides.json：一個逐個 commit SHA 對返一套正常字眼嘅
對照表，build-changelog.mjs 生成嗰陣會先睇呢度，睇唔到先揸返原本嘅 commit
字。搵晒成部歷史入面仲有漏嘅 commit，逐個填好。

加咗 scripts/check-private-terms.mjs：同現有嘅 check-published-text.mjs 做
兄弟，代號清單擺喺 repo 外面，用 WORLDLENS_PRIVATE_TERMS_FILE 呢個環境變數
指路。冇設呢個變數 - 即係公開機器同 CI 嗰啲情況 - 佢淨係印一句話咗過就收工，
exit 0。有設嘅話就掃晒成個 repo 嘅檔案，撞到就報返檔名同行數然後 fail；
仲會（唔會令個 run 爆）額外報埋最近 200 個 commit 標題入面重有幾多個仲用緊
舊字眼，指去 overrides 個檔度執。喺 design/package.json 加咗
check:private-terms，AGENTS.md 記低點用，仲加咗個 vitest 包住去驗個
「冇檔就跳過」嘅路線。

驗證過：擺一份真嘅代號清單落去，個 guard 喺呢棵樹度乾乾淨淨；特登加返一個
代號入去，佢即刻指出邊個檔邊一行。build-changelog.mjs --check、
lint-workflows.mjs、個網站嘅文章 bundle 驗證都仲係綠;新加同改咗名嗰啲測試
喺 vitest 底下都過晒。

d5faa910e6787af0658d1cb4436a5a0bdb41d014.subject: Record the release, and what was proven about it
d5faa910e6787af0658d1cb4436a5a0bdb41d014.body:
v1.0.1888, non-draft, target d18a7fc9, CI green on all six jobs. The evidence
worth keeping is not the job names: the plugins zip was downloaded from the
release, the paper jar opened, and its embedded webapp checked - 32 Material
Design 3 colour roles, 138 references, no surviving upstream literals, and the
same stylesheet filename the local build emitted.

Also recorded: the jars read 5.23-1 rather than 5.23-material-design-3-1 because CI checks
the submodule out detached and upstream's version function has no branch name to
append. Same commit, different label, and worth knowing before somebody reads the
difference as two different builds.

The not-done section now says what the evidence does not cover: this is byte-level
proof that the stylesheet ships, not a photograph of how it looks.

出咗 v1.0.1888，落載返個 jar 拆開睇過，M3 真係入面。但淨係證到啲 bytes 有，未影
過相，所以照寫低。

aaa44b016d8a6c60c21dd6964131455b1080df27.subject: Build BlueMap from the fork, so the map ships the new interface
aaa44b016d8a6c60c21dd6964131455b1080df27.body:
The Material Design 3 webapp existed and nothing consumed it. The jars embed the
webapp, so which checkout the jars are built from is what decides the interface a
published map shows - and every build path still read the upstream submodule.

tools/build-jars.mjs, build-jars.yml, render-world.yml and render-private-world.yml
now read vendor/BlueMap-Material. The path and the repository are single exported
constants that the packager's own validator consumes, so a manifest written from
one source and checked against another cannot pass; that validator had a second
hardcoded copy of the path, which is exactly how the two would have drifted.
CI_WORKFLOW_TEMPLATE_VERSION goes to 3 because an already-bootstrapped repository
needs the new template and an older application must not hand back the old one.

Proven by measuring the artifact rather than the configuration. A local build
produced cli-5.23-material-design-3-1-shadow.jar, and the webapp.zip inside it carries 32
Material Design 3 colour roles across 138 references, 25 focus rings, 36 elevation
references, 20 reduced-motion blocks, no upstream colour literals, and Quicksand
intact. The version string is the second tell: Gradle stamped 5.23-material-design-3-1,
which only the fork produces.

vendor/BlueMap stays as the unmodified upstream reference to port from, and
CONTRIBUTING.md now says which checkout does which job. Two full checkouts is real
disk and real clone time; retiring one is recorded on the roadmap rather than done
quietly here.

Also honest about what is still red: lint-workflows.mjs reports twelve
release-boundary problems on main already, and diffing its output with and without
this change is byte-identical, so none of them are new.

改用 fork 起 jar，唔係上游。webapp 係包喺 jar 入面嘅，所以起邊個 checkout 就決定
地圖出街係咩樣。冇靠睇 config 就話得咗，係拆開個 jar 睇真嘅：32 個 M3 色角色、
138 處引用、一個上游舊色都冇。
